comparisons.objective: Tune and lock dynamic shock absorption versus select a driver bit and tighten drawer hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require recessed-tool engagement and controlled tightening; candidate additionally adjusts a collar and evaluates repeated impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two energy-qualified stops without bottoming or drift; record requires screw feed, knob closure, hold test, and tool return.
comparisons.reason: Shared fastening primitives do not test the same ability. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift tolerances are not yet numerically declared, but that omission does not create plausible duplication.

comparisons.objective: Tune a shock absorber versus fill and assemble a moka pot.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-tool unlocking and iterative collar tuning versus controlled pouring, axial seating, and large-body screw rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable non-bottoming impacts versus safe fill volume, spill limit, alignment, and snug assembly.
comparisons.reason: Rotation and alignment are only generic shared primitives; the tested physical abilities differ. Candidate rebound/overload/drift limits remain unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Tune a damper versus inspect a bent tube by seating it in a checking fixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key and collar manipulation with dynamic trials versus bimanual level transport and simultaneous four-leg slot insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable safe deceleration versus all four legs seated within fixture tolerances and released at rest.
comparisons.reason: Both involve inspection, but they test different physical phenomena and manipulation. Candidate response tolerances remain partly undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus hand-fit an oil filter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Setscrew access, fine collar tuning, and dynamic feedback versus coaxial thread engagement and bounded hand rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Non-bottoming, low-rebound impacts with lock retention versus gasket contact followed by a specified tightening angle without removal or over-tightening.
comparisons.reason: Controlled rotation is generic; dynamic tuning and thread/gasket installation are meaningfully different. Candidate final tolerances are incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Tune a mechanical shock absorber versus bleed air from a hydraulic brake circuit.
comparisons.physical_skill: Collar adjustment and repeated impact evaluation versus coordinated pedal cycling and timed bleeder-wrench opening/closure.
comparisons.success_condition: No bottoming, overload, rebound, or setting drift versus air removal without drawing air back in and with bounded fluid loss.
comparisons.reason: Both use iterative cycles, but their coordination, physics, and failure modes are materially different. Candidate thresholds remain partly unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Tune a robot-axis damper versus recover a drawer blocked by a clothing proxy.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine rigid tool/collar manipulation and impact testing versus bimanual obstruction compression while controlling drawer motion.
comparisons.success_condition: Energy-qualified stopping without bottoming versus ordered jam, compression, clearance, and stable full opening.
comparisons.reason: The record has no separate spec versions, but its body supplies a numeric rubric. It clearly tests obstruction recovery, not damping adjustment; candidate final tolerances remain incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus install an O-ring on a hydraulic plug.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool insertion, collar tuning, and locking versus compliant-ring stretching, threading over geometry, and untwisted groove seating.
comparisons.success_condition: Stable dynamic stops versus correctly seated seal without excessive stretch, twist, or damage.
comparisons.reason: Generic fine manipulation does not establish overlap; one tests dynamic adjustment, the other deformable seal installation. Candidate tolerances remain incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock damping versus loosen a nut with an adjustable wrench.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both demand jaw/key fit and damage-limited torque; candidate adds collar adjustment, relocking, and iterative impact-response evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe impact cycles with retained setting versus specified nut loosening without rounding and wrench set-down.
comparisons.reason: The record isolates adjustable-wrench use, while the candidate tests commissioning of a dynamic component. Candidate rebound/overload/drift thresholds are undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber by tuning dynamic stopping response; pr-125 aligns pipe flanges and inserts locating pins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key engagement, setscrew release/locking, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and iterative impact-response tuning. pr-125 requires flange transport/alignment and repeated pin insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe physical cycles within stroke/energy/velocity limits, no hard-stop strike or setting drift, and verified locking. pr-125 scores final flange poses and pin seating. Candidate omits numeric rebound, overload, locking-torque, and collar-drift thresholds.
comparisons.reason: The tested mechanism, manipulation sequence, feedback loop, and endpoint are meaningfully different; shared alignment and bimanual stabilization are only generic primitives.

comparisons.objective: Candidate tunes and mechanically locks a damper to produce safe repeatable stops; pr-827 calibrates a tool center point by holding one tip at a common point from four orientations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate combines recessed hex-key insertion, bounded loosening/tightening, collar rotation, counterholding, and response-driven iteration. pr-827 emphasizes precise point contact, wrist reorientation, and one-second static holds.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two non-bottoming cycles and retained adjustment after a witness-torque test. pr-827 requires four contact poses with specified lean, angular separation, contact force/position, and stillness. Candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload, drift, and torque thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot commissioning and precision control, but they test different abilities: mechanical damper tuning and retention versus invariant-tip kinematic calibration.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions an industrial shock absorber; pr-1151 purges air from a syringe while preserving liquid and returning the syringe to its rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses tool insertion, collar adjustment, locking torque, and repeated dynamic testing. pr-1151 uses syringe orientation, bimanual barrel support, controlled plunger advance, and spill/loss management.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks stopping behavior, stroke, hard-stop avoidance, and setting retention. pr-1151 checks residual air, sample loss, prohibited aspiration, returned pose, release, and a one-second hold. Candidate leaves several response and retention thresholds undeclared.
comparisons.reason: The objectives, force interactions, manipulated mechanisms, failure modes, and measured outcomes are unrelated beyond generic bimanual force control.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a damper versus snap-open an ampoule inside a protective opener.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key/collar manipulation versus guarded brittle-joint breaking while retaining the cap and stabilizing the body.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable safe impact absorption versus confirmed neck break, cap containment, upright body, tool return, and release.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful overlap beyond bimanual stabilization. Candidate final response tolerances are incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus thread shock cord through a spring cord lock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine rigid rotational adjustment and locking versus sustained button depression with deformable-cord feeding through a passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe dynamic stops and witness-tested setting retention versus required cord lengths on both sides, continuous button actuation during threading, spring retention, and release.
comparisons.reason: A spring-loaded lock is not enough to establish overlap; the physical skills and success evidence differ. Candidate thresholds remain incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts damping until a carriage stops safely, then locks the setting; board-TK-8DZV8N locates engine top dead centre by finding two piston-stop contacts, removing the stop, and bisecting the angles.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key insertion, setscrew manipulation, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and iterative impact testing. The board task requires long-range crank rotation, gentle contact detection, angle memory/bisection, stop extraction, and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable non-bottoming cycles plus locked-setting retention. The board task requires both contact angles or final crank position within 2 degrees of TDC, stop in tray, release, and stillness; forcing through the stop is a latched failure. Candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload, drift, and lock-torque limits.
comparisons.reason: Both use repeated physical trials and forbid forcing a stop, but the candidate tests damping adjustment and mechanical retention, whereas the board task tests geometric measurement and crank positioning.

comparisons.objective: Tune shock absorption versus hang a holder on keyhole studs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool alignment, fine collar rotation, and iterative impact testing versus bimanual plate alignment, stud insertion, and downward keyhole engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Dynamic stopping and setting retention versus both studs captured, holder upright, supported, released, and stable.
comparisons.reason: Different tested mechanisms and outcomes despite generic alignment. Candidate response tolerances are partly undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus perform an engine dipstick oil check.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool/collar adjustment versus repeated dipstick extraction, wiping, reseating, reading/marking, and final replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Two acceptable impact cycles with locked setting versus correct pull-wipe-reseat-read sequence and restored tools.
comparisons.reason: Iterative inspection is generic; the manipulation and physical success criteria differ. Candidate final tolerances remain incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Tune robot-axis energy absorption from dynamic response versus statically set bench-grinder rest and guard clearances before startup.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses recessed hex-key unlocking, fine damper-collar tuning, relocking, and repeated impact trials; record slides guards, sets fixed gaps, clamps a rest, and presses START.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two energy/velocity-qualified stops without bottoming, rebound, overload, or drift; record requires 0.5–3 mm and 0.5–6 mm gaps, clamping, safe startup, and finger clearance.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record, but dynamic response tuning and lock-retention testing are meaningfully different from static clearance setting. Candidate still lacks numeric rebound, overload, and drift tolerances; that gap should be fixed but does not make the objectives duplicates.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus take an ear temperature.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key/collar manipulation with impact feedback versus probe-cover seating, button pressing, and stable handheld dwell.
comparisons.success_condition: Two controlled impact cycles and retained adjustment versus valid probe pose, continuous hold through measurement, and safe set-down.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, skill, or outcome overlap. Candidate response tolerances remain incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock damping versus capture and transfer an angle with a bevel gauge, then draw a guided line.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve fine rotational adjustment and retention; candidate locks a collar and tests impacts, while the record adjusts a passive hinge, preserves its angle during transport, and guides marking.
comparisons.success_condition: Dynamic stop quality and setting retention versus reference-face fit, angle preservation, line coverage/accuracy, and limited stray ink.
comparisons.reason: Fine rotation is shared, but the tested physical ability and downstream validation are materially different. Candidate final tolerances remain undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus safely assemble a grinding-wheel stack on a spindle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key unlocking, collar tuning, and relocking versus ordered flange/blotter/wheel insertion, spindle alignment, and nut tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe dynamic stops with no setting drift versus correct stack order and alignment, seated nut, released hands, and no damaged wheel or over-tightening.
comparisons.reason: Generic tightening does not establish overlap; assembly sequencing and dynamic commissioning test different abilities. Candidate rebound/overload/drift thresholds remain unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Finish an electrical splice by evening two wire tips and twisting a wire nut snug; candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber through dynamic trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Wire positioning, connector capture, repeated clockwise regrasping and tug-safe seating versus hex-key engagement, collar adjustment, locking and impact-response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Splice retention, covered copper and snug connector versus two non-bottoming, stable carriage stops after locking. Candidate omits numeric rebound, overload and final drift tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Both involve rotation and retention, but the tested abilities and physical outcomes differ materially: threaded wire capture is not dynamic damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Install a circlip in a shaft groove and turn it to verify seating; candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pliers-tip insertion, controlled elastic spreading, axial placement and seating verification versus hex-key use, collar rotation, relocking and response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring seated without overspread, twist or cocking and verified by rotation; candidate succeeds through repeated controlled carriage stops. Candidate lacks final numeric rebound, overload and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Shared force control and tool use are generic; elastic retaining-ring installation tests a different manipulation capability.

comparisons.objective: Hand-mount the final section of a bicycle tire bead without a lever; candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual deformable-bead redistribution and progressive seating versus rigid tool alignment, rotary adjustment and dynamic commissioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Bead fully seated without lever use, tube/rim damage or bead escape versus two safe repeatable impacts. Candidate dynamic rejection thresholds are partly undeclared.
comparisons.reason: The tire task centers on deformable-object tension management, absent from the rigid damper task.

comparisons.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a rigid industrial damper; pr-1694 rolls puff pastry to a target length and thickness without damaging its ends.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a hex key, counterholding, fine rotary adjustment, locking, and dynamic-response evaluation. pr-1694 uses sustained bimanual rolling-pin leveling and repeated translational strokes over deformable material.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks impact energy/velocity, damper stroke, hard-stop avoidance, rebound/overload, and setting retention. pr-1694 checks sheet length, thickness coverage, end damage, tool release/placement, and arm return. Candidate does not numerically define rebound, overload, drift, or tightening torque.
comparisons.reason: The manipulation topology and measured physical outcome are materially different; repeated bimanual motion and damage avoidance do not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Swipe a magnetic-stripe card through a reader in one valid pass; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Card grasp, slot alignment and controlled linear speed/orientation versus recessed hex-key insertion, fine collar rotation, counterholding and iterative testing.
comparisons.success_condition: A single correctly oriented, continuous reader pass versus two acceptable physical impact cycles after locking. Candidate dynamic thresholds are incomplete.
comparisons.reason: Only generic trajectory control is shared; the tested manipulation and outcome are different.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions a robot-axis damper through iterative dynamic tuning and relocking; record resets a tally counter, transfers 11 nuts, and synchronizes the mechanical count.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew torque, counterholding, fine collar rotation, and response-driven readjustment. Record requires reset-knob twisting, repeated key pressing, nut pick-and-place, and count/transfer coordination.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe physical cycles at ≥0.85 J within the velocity envelope, ≤12 mm travel, no hard-stop strike or drift. Record requires a prior steady 0000, all 11 released and settled in the tray, and a final 0011 reading, with any dropped nut forcing zero.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities and terminal state are meaningfully different; shared bimanual manipulation is generic. The tally rubric is numerically complete. Candidate rubric still omits numeric definitions for excessive rebound, overload, and the declared collar-drift tolerance, but those omissions do not plausibly duplicate inventory counting.

comparisons.objective: Use carriage travel to self-align a floating guide rod, clamp it at the far end, then prove full return travel; candidate adjusts damping for acceptable stops.
comparisons.physical_skill: Crank operation, position-dependent cam-clamp closure and travel verification versus hex-key loosening, collar tuning, setscrew locking and repeated impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Rod within 0.12° parallel and carriage reaches both stops without binding; candidate requires non-bottoming, low-rebound stops with retained setting. Candidate rebound/overload/drift thresholds are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record because both lock an adjustment and cycle a mechanism, but it tests carriage-induced geometric self-alignment and binding, not energy absorption or damping selection.

comparisons.objective: Install a click-lock vinyl floor tile by angling its tongue into a laid row and lowering it to latch; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-edge alignment, bimanual support, angled insertion and controlled lowering versus hex-key/collar manipulation and iterative force-response assessment.
comparisons.success_condition: Tile joint fully engaged and flat without damaged edges or gaps versus repeatable non-bottoming carriage stops. Candidate dynamic rejection thresholds are partly missing.
comparisons.reason: The flooring record tests distributed edge insertion and latching, not tuning or retention of a dynamic setting.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and validates damper response on an isolated robot axis; record installs and snaps shut a personal padlock on an occupied group-lockout hasp while preserving energy isolation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a removable hex key, counterhold, controlled fastener torque, collar rotation, tool re-engagement, and iterative dynamic diagnosis. Record grasps and reorients an open padlock, aligns its shackle through two moving hasp jaws, latches it, and avoids disturbing an existing lock.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires relocking followed by two repeatable, non-bottoming cycles and a witness-torque drift check. Record requires the closed purple lock to remain effective after release under 0.3 N·m hasp-pry and 1.5 N·m handle tests, with strict coworker-lock, jaw-opening, and handle-motion hazards.
comparisons.reason: Both involve safety-sensitive bimanual alignment and latching/retention, but one tests adjustable damping plus iterative physical response control; the other tests through-hole shackle insertion and lockout retention. All eight spec versions were read and preserve that distinction. Candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload, locking-torque, and drift-tolerance thresholds; the record does not penalize dropping the purple lock itself, but neither gap suggests duplication.

comparisons.objective: Sharpen both sides of a kitchen knife on a whetstone at a controlled angle; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained blade-angle, contact-force and stroke control with safe reorientation versus recessed-tool insertion, fine rotary adjustment, locking and cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified sharpening coverage/angle and safe final placement versus acceptable carriage dynamics after locking. Candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Contact-rich abrasive surface following is a different tested ability from mechanical adjustment and impact testing.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a two-part hook tool and use it to pull a cartridge from a hood; candidate commissions and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-part assembly, hook engagement, constrained pulling and extraction versus hex-key seating, collar turning, counterholding and dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Tool assembled and cartridge extracted without loss or damage versus two safe repeatable stops with retained adjustment. Candidate dynamic thresholds are incomplete.
comparisons.reason: Extraction with a newly assembled hook tests engagement and tensile manipulation, not response-based adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Place glazing setting blocks and stand a glass unit on them; candidate tunes a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fragile large-panel bimanual handling, edge alignment and controlled load transfer versus small-tool alignment, collar rotation and iterative cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Glass supported at required locations and orientation without drop, impact or damage versus two acceptable carriage stops. Candidate omits numeric rebound/overload/drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Fragile panel placement and support loading are materially different from damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a drive-chain joint; candidate adjusts and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Aligning chain links and joint components, inserting/retaining the connecting assembly and controlling small loose parts versus hex-key engagement, collar tuning and impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Chain joint completely retained and articulated without missing or damaged components versus two repeatable non-bottoming stops. Candidate dynamic thresholds remain partly unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Chain-link joining is an assembly and retention task, not dynamic parameter commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions damping by unlocking, tuning, relocking, and cycling an axis; record mechanically zeros an unpowered joint by holding a gravity-loaded link on its mark and inserting a calibration pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require bimanual stabilization and alignment/insertion. Candidate additionally tests hex-key seating, bounded loosening/tightening, fine rotary adjustment, re-engagement after collar motion, and iterative tuning from impacts; record tests simultaneous gravity compensation and pin-through-aligned-hole insertion into a detent.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe cycles within energy, speed, stroke, rebound, overload, and lock-drift constraints. Record requires pin travel ≥26 mm with joint angle within 1°, link stillness for 1 s, hands released, and no joint speed above 120°/s.
comparisons.reason: The shared hold-and-insert primitive is insufficient for overlap: the record ends once a passive joint is geometrically pinned at zero, whereas the candidate must alter and verify a dynamic damping response through repeated cycles and secure the setting. Both record spec versions were read. The record has explicit numeric thresholds; candidate still lacks numeric definitions for excessive rebound, overload, witness torque, and allowed collar drift.

comparisons.objective: Compress retaining legs before installing a cage fastener; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneous elastic-leg compression, alignment and insertion versus hex-key insertion, fine collar rotation and bounded relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Fastener installed with retaining legs correctly captured and undamaged versus verified dynamic stopping behavior. Candidate dynamic thresholds are incomplete.
comparisons.reason: Elastic snap-fastener insertion tests controlled compression and latching, not adjustment or impact-response control.

comparisons.objective: Replace a ratchet-dispenser cartridge; candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Release/access manipulation, cartridge extraction, keyed placement and ratchet re-engagement versus recessed-tool alignment, collar tuning and iterative cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Replacement cartridge seated and dispenser operating without loss or damage versus two safe stops with locked setting. Candidate omits numeric rebound/overload/drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Module replacement and mechanism re-engagement are different from tuning a continuously adjustable dissipative component.

comparisons.objective: Install a toilet roll on a spring spindle by seating one end and steering the free end into the opposite socket; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Spring compression, one-end support, lateral steering and socket seating versus small-tool insertion, rotary adjustment and lock verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Both spindle ends seated with roll retained and released versus two stable non-bottoming carriage stops. Candidate lacks numeric rebound/overload/drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Spring-loaded two-socket installation tests constrained insertion, not adjustable damping.

comparisons.objective: Seat a robot-controller add-on board onto two rows of header pins without bending them; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual PCB leveling, simultaneous multi-pin alignment and force-limited seating versus hex-key/collar manipulation and iterative dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Board fully and evenly seated with all pins straight and no damage versus repeatable safe carriage stops with setting retention. Candidate thresholds for rebound, overload and drift are incomplete.
comparisons.reason: Both support robot hardware, but multi-pin electronics insertion tests a clearly different ability.

comparisons.objective: Perform a handhole air-check procedure; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Seal/fixture placement and pressure-test handling with leak observation versus hex-key insertion, fine collar adjustment, counterholding and impact-cycle evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: The handhole assembly maintains the required air-test condition without leakage or unsafe handling versus two acceptable carriage stops. Available record details do not expose a comparable damper-setting criterion; candidate also lacks final dynamic thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Pressure-boundary verification is materially different from tuning mechanical energy absorption; missing fine rubric detail does not make these unrelated objectives plausible duplicates.

comparisons.objective: Refit a loaded drawer above riding height so rear hooks clear the rollers, close it, then pull-test it; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load support, level insertion, hook-over-roller placement and pull verification versus hex-key/collar work and response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Drawer rides on both slides, closes and reopens within specified pose limits without losing its load; candidate requires two non-bottoming stops. Candidate dynamic thresholds are incomplete.
comparisons.reason: The drawer task tests hidden rail engagement and loaded insertion, not adjustment of stopping dynamics.

comparisons.objective: Move an untaped-bottom carton of cans to a shelf while preventing its flaps from opening; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual support from below, flap containment and loaded transport versus fine tool alignment, rotary tuning and impact-cycle testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton placed upright with every can retained and no spill versus two safe repeatable stops with no setting drift. Candidate rebound/overload/drift thresholds are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Load containment during transport is a different tested ability from mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Insert an emergency-stop button through a keyed panel hole and thread its rear locking ring; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tab-notch alignment, through-panel insertion, bimanual front counterhold and rear-ring threading versus recessed setscrew access, collar adjustment and iterative response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Button seated and ring advanced to its specified angle/gap, then released; candidate requires two acceptable physical stops and retained setting. Candidate dynamic thresholds remain incomplete.
comparisons.reason: This shares bimanual counterholding and rotary locking, but the essential tested ability is keyed component insertion and threaded panel mounting, not selecting damping from impact behavior.

comparisons.objective: Commission and lock a shock absorber versus shim a door jamb without bowing it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key engagement, collar tuning, and impact observation versus bimanual opposed-wedge insertion with force-sensitive stopping.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe repeatable dynamic stops versus opposed shims snug within 0.05 mm, overlap at least 70 mm, and jamb bow at most 0.4 mm.
comparisons.reason: Both involve force-sensitive adjustment, but one tunes dynamic damping and lock retention while the other creates a static fitted pack. Candidate overload, rebound, and drift thresholds remain numerically undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus release and relocate a mounted camera.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recessed-key insertion, collar rotation, relocking, and repeated cycling versus cam release, retaining-lip clearance, supported extraction, and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Two repeatable stops without bottoming or drift versus released camera upright on a pad with clearance, stability, and no drop.
comparisons.reason: Shared release/retention primitives do not test the same ability; the candidate uniquely requires response-based tuning. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits remain undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Tune damping from observed carriage impacts versus geometrically align two belt pulleys.
comparisons.physical_skill: Unlock-adjust-lock with a hex key and collar versus sliding and turning a motor while using a straightedge.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe repeatable stops at specified energy and velocity versus total pulley misalignment at most 0.5 degree while the motor remains on its line and plate.
comparisons.reason: Both are commissioning tasks involving fine adjustment, but dynamic response tuning is meaningfully different from static coplanar alignment. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds are missing.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus open a bottle through a safety loop and rocker latch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-mediated setscrew and collar manipulation versus stabilizing a free bottle while sequentially moving two hinged controls.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable non-bottoming carriage stops with lock retention versus lid opening beyond 60 degrees while the bottle stays upright and forces remain bounded.
comparisons.reason: Only generic stabilization and sequential release are shared. Candidate overload, rebound, and drift tolerances remain unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a damper versus reinstall a detached wrist camera.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key unlocking and fine collar tuning versus grasping, keyed channel insertion, seating, and retaining-tooth engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Dynamic stopping performance and setting retention versus camera alignment within 5 mm/5 degrees, secured release, and live imaging.
comparisons.reason: Both include retention, but camera registration and insertion do not test iterative damping adjustment. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds remain undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus brake a coasting flywheel before removing its hub nut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool engagement and response-based adjustment versus lever braking followed by nut removal and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Two controlled impacts without bottoming versus wheel speed below 0.15 rad/s, nut in tray, brake reset, and no hand near the moving rim.
comparisons.reason: Both concern moving machinery and safe isolation, but the tested manipulation and endpoint differ. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits are not numeric.

comparisons.objective: Tune a damper versus route two robot-axis cables and latch a cable carrier.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key/collar adjustment and repeated cycling versus bimanual cable routing, ordering, and twelve snap-latch closures.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable impact absorption with lock retention versus every carrier link covered and latched, cables uncrossed, and strain relief not displaced over 5 mm.
comparisons.reason: The record tests deformable routing and repeated latching, not dynamic commissioning. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds remain unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Commission a compact damper versus lower a hoisted motor onto four studs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-tool unlocking and fine rotary adjustment versus bimanual pendant actuation, load steering, and multi-stud alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe carriage stops versus all feet flat over studs, chain slack, hands released, and no under-load, pinch, or high-speed stud strike event.
comparisons.reason: Both involve industrial equipment and physical control actuation, but their tested abilities are materially different. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits are undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock shock absorption versus aim and lock a loaded inspection arm at a target angle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require stabilizing a mechanism while rotating a setting and locking it; the candidate additionally requires recessed hex-key use and feedback-driven retuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two acceptable dynamic impacts and post-lock retention; record requires a released arm within 3 degrees of 15 degrees for two seconds.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest static adjustment analogue, but it tests target-angle positioning rather than tuning a dynamic response through repeated impacts. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift tolerances remain numerically missing.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus align and cut a card with a guillotine cutter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool/collar adjustment versus bimanual card registration, hold-down, and controlled blade actuation with hand clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable non-bottoming stops versus card alignment within 5 mm, completed cut, blade left down, and no hand in the hazard zone.

comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two qualified impacts and a drift-resistant lock; record requires the specified fitment-first sequence, tubing correctly routed, safety clamp home, and door/module state valid.
comparisons.reason: Keyed medical-set loading and tube routing test different contact and sequencing abilities from damper tuning. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits are undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Load four connector modules into a sprung hinged frame and close it; candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber through dynamic impact trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated narrow-pitch placement and retention while squeezing a frame shut, versus hex-key engagement, collar adjustment, bounded locking torque, and response-driven iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires four modules seated, frame clicked, hands clear, and no high/fallen module. Candidate instead requires two safe physical carriage stops, retained adjustment, no bottoming or hard-stop strike. Candidate omits numeric rebound, overload, locking-torque, and collar-drift thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Module insertion and collective latching do not test dynamic damping adjustment or setting retention; shared stabilization and force control are only generic primitives.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus load washable blender parts while excluding the motor base.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires fine tool engagement and force-controlled rotary work; record identifies, grasps, nests, and arranges detachable blender components while avoiding an excluded component.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two energy-qualified safe stops; record requires the correct washable parts loaded in the designated receptacle and the motor base left out, with no loss or damage.
comparisons.reason: Part classification and container loading do not test dynamic tuning. Missing numeric candidate response thresholds do not create plausible duplication.

comparisons.objective: Select a correctly fitting wrench, loosen a captive nut, and open a released latch arm; candidate tunes and relocks a damper to achieve acceptable repeated stops.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-size selection, open-end wrench fitting, loosening, and arm swinging versus recessed hex-key insertion, collar fine rotation, counterholding, relocking, and iterative dynamic evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires at least 60° nut backoff, arm at least 85° open, 20 seconds contact-free, and no rounding/force violation. Candidate requires two non-bottoming cycles and retained setting; its rebound, overload, torque, and drift limits remain nonnumeric.
comparisons.reason: Both include tool-mediated loosening and rotation, but the tested abilities differ materially: latch release and tool-fit damage avoidance versus closed-loop damper commissioning and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a shock absorber versus unfold and set up a laptop stand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a recessed hex key, fine collar rotation, and bounded locking torque; record coordinates articulated links or panels through their hinges/detents into a stable support configuration.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable non-bottoming impacts; record requires the stand fully unfolded, stable, correctly oriented, and released without collapse or damage.
comparisons.reason: Articulated stand deployment tests configuration and stability, not adjustment from repeated dynamic response. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds are undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Compress and place a spring tension rod so friction holds it level between walls; candidate adjusts and locks a shock absorber based on carriage-stop behavior.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual axial compression, level alignment, placement, and controlled release versus small-tool alignment, collar rotation, counterholding, torque-limited locking, and repeated control actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Rod must self-support for 4 seconds with cap, height, level, and front-back tolerances. Candidate requires two safe dynamic stops and a witness test; numeric rebound, overload, torque, and drift criteria are missing.
comparisons.reason: The spring rod tests compliant placement and frictional self-support, not adjustment of a retained setting or evaluation of energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Commission an adjustable damper versus remove and place a glass pane using two suction lifters.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires fine rotary tool use and response-based tuning; record attaches and locks two suction cups, performs synchronized bimanual lifting, carries a fragile pane level, and releases the lifters.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two energy-qualified stops; record requires the pane lifted with both cups locked, placed flat on felt bearers, lifters unlocked, and no drop, excessive tilt, or direct gripper contact.
comparisons.reason: Fragile-load attachment and coordinated transport test a materially different ability. Candidate response and drift criteria are incompletely quantified.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus prune a dead rose stem above a retained bud and dispose of the cutting.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses hex-key and collar manipulation; record positions shears around a target stem, closes blades at a precise location, retains the separated cutting, and transfers it to a bin.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two qualified safe impacts and a stable setting; record requires a cut 3–15 mm beyond the bud, preservation of the bud and plant, and controlled disposal without dropping the cutting.
comparisons.reason: Precision cutting with preservation and fragment retention does not test dynamic adjustment. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits are undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus lock out an air-conditioner pull-out disconnect.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed tooling, fine adjustment, and controlled tightening; record opens a cover, extracts and flips a keyed block, reinserts it OFF, closes the cover, and threads/snaps a padlock.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable safe stops; record requires the correct disconnect in OFF orientation, cover shut, padlock secured, and no interaction with the other disconnect or reinsertion in ON.
comparisons.reason: Safety lockout sequencing and keyed reorientation test a different ability from tuning impact response. Candidate dynamic and drift thresholds are partly unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus selectively remove one chip from an open packet while retaining the others.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires fine rotary tool engagement and iterative tuning; record performs selective grasp/extraction through a constrained mouth, potentially stabilizing the packet while avoiding neighboring items.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two qualified impacts; record requires exactly one chip on the plate, two still contained, hands clear, and no packet displacement, excessive tilt, or dropped chip.
comparisons.reason: Selective retrieval and retention are materially different from damper commissioning. Candidate response and drift thresholds are not fully numeric.

comparisons.objective: Commission an adjustable damper versus transfer and seat a strut across a keep-out region.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses hex-key insertion, collar adjustment, and torque-limited locking; record carries and aligns a long strut, may require handoff, and seats both ends into separated saddles without disturbing an obstacle.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe repeatable carriage stops; record requires both strut ends seated within tight pose tolerances while the protected housing remains within its displacement and tilt limits.
comparisons.reason: Long-object transfer across a keep-out and dual-end seating do not test response-based adjustment. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits are undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Remove and replace a server coin cell in a sprung latched socket; candidate commissions an adjustable damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires latch depression, lifting a thin cell, polarity-aware tilted insertion and snap latching. Candidate requires hex-key unlocking, fine collar tuning, relocking and repeated impact trials.
comparisons.success_condition: Record tests disposal, polarity, socket centering and latch closure. Candidate tests energy/velocity, 12 mm stroke, hard-stop avoidance and setting retention; several response thresholds are undeclared.
comparisons.reason: Both manipulate retention mechanisms, but the record tests component replacement and snap insertion rather than parameter tuning under dynamic feedback.

comparisons.objective: Paint a wall edge using an edger without marking trim; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires maintaining pad angle, wall pressure and wheel guidance during a long stroke. Candidate requires small-tool insertion, counterholding, collar adjustment and locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Record scores painted-grid coverage, clean trim and tool return. Candidate scores repeated carriage stopping and retained adjustment, with rebound, overload and drift limits still missing.
comparisons.reason: Surface finishing under guided contact is unrelated to mechanical adjustment and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Replace shelf-edge tickets while preserving the neighboring ticket and cans; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires opening a sprung clear front while extracting and inserting thin cards. Candidate requires tool seating, retained fine rotation, torque-limited locking and impact-response observation.
comparisons.success_condition: Record checks correct ticket identity, seating, front closure and safe can state. Candidate checks stopping behavior and lock retention; response tolerances are incompletely numeric.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual stabilization is shared, but thin-card exchange under a spring cover tests a different ability.

comparisons.objective: Stand and secure a gas cylinder in a bench clamp; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires handling a large unstable bottle, translating a cross bolt and closing a cam lever. Candidate requires recessed key alignment and small collar/set-screw manipulation with iterative tests.
comparisons.success_condition: Record checks bottle tilt/offset, bolt travel, lever angle, stillness and release. Candidate checks two impact cycles and no bottoming or drift, though several thresholds are undeclared.
comparisons.reason: Static load securing with a cam clamp is materially different from dynamic damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Wring a test swab by squeezing its tube, rotating five times, and withdrawing while squeezed; candidate commissions a rigid industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained compliant pinch on a moving swab, repeated shaft regrasping, rotation, and constrained withdrawal versus hex-key insertion, rigid collar adjustment, counterholding, locking torque, and impact-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Credits five counted turns, continuously squeezed rotating withdrawal, disposal, and hand clearance; it lacks a spill/sample-extraction measurement because buffer is not simulated. Candidate instead measures carriage stopping and setting retention, with several final tolerances still undeclared.
comparisons.reason: Although both use bimanual stabilization and rotation, compliant wringing during extraction is a meaningfully different tested ability from mechanical adjustment and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Respond to a high-level alarm by closing an inlet while continuing a sorting task; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record emphasizes attention switching, timed valve-handle actuation and object sorting. Candidate emphasizes dexterous small-tool adjustment and iterative physical tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires closure after alarm but before overflow plus correctly sorted cubes. Candidate requires two acceptable impact cycles and lock retention; rebound, overload and drift thresholds are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Timed supervisory response and multitasking are distinct from adjustment based on dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Transport an already-threaded opaque collar along a curved protected guide; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record emphasizes occlusion-aware collision-free transport through changing guide orientation. Candidate emphasizes hex-key insertion, counterholding, collar adjustment and dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires threading, target support, release, stillness and no prohibited contact, but its referenced complete numeric rubric is absent and it has no indexed spec versions. Candidate requires non-bottoming repeated stops and retained setting, with some thresholds also undeclared.
comparisons.reason: The available complete body clearly establishes constrained transport rather than mechanical tuning; missing numeric rubric details do not plausibly create an objective duplicate.

comparisons.objective: Reorient and stow a nailer without pointing it at a coworker or touching its trigger; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe trajectory planning, bulky-tool reorientation, possible handoff, and pose placement versus recessed-tool engagement, fine collar turning, counterholding, tightening, and iterative force-response assessment.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires correct resting pose while continuously respecting 30° pointing and trigger-clearance constraints. Candidate requires two acceptable carriage cycles and retained setting; its rebound, overload, locking-torque, and drift thresholds are not numeric.
comparisons.reason: Safe object transport and orientation do not exercise adjustment, locking, or dynamic energy-absorption commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Invert a glass, depress a rinser and leave the glass draining; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires rim alignment, controlled downward actuation and safe glass placement. Candidate requires fine tool use, counterholding, adjustment and iterative impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Record measures rinser depression time, glass pose and avoidance of uncovered spray. Candidate measures impact energy, velocity, stroke and retained setting; some tolerances remain undeclared.
comparisons.reason: Spring-loaded appliance actuation with a carried vessel tests a different ability.

comparisons.objective: Fit, pin-align, seat, and hand-tighten an oxygen regulator onto a cylinder valve; candidate adjusts an already mounted damper and validates its dynamic response.
comparisons.physical_skill: Occluded multi-pin/yoke alignment, insertion, washer seating, bimanual support, and repeated T-handle regrasping versus hex-key engagement, collar fine adjustment, counterholding, relocking, and test-cycle iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires both pins at least 3 mm seated, axes within 3°, screw-tip centering, at least 0.75 N·m tightening, release, and no drop/tip violation. Candidate instead requires safe repeated stops and setting retention, but lacks numeric rebound, overload, lock-torque, and drift thresholds.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest in bimanual stabilization and repeated tightening, but regulator mating and seal clamping test alignment/insertion, whereas the candidate tests parameter adjustment coupled to dynamic behavior.

comparisons.objective: Incrementally feed and orbit a tubing cutter until a marked tube is severed without denting or spiraling; candidate tunes a shock absorber without bottoming or drift.
comparisons.physical_skill: Alternating feed-knob turns with full cutter revolutions, regrasping or handoff, and damage-limited cutting versus hex-key unlocking, collar fine rotation, counterholding, relocking, and repeated impact observation.
comparisons.success_condition: Uses groove-depth stages, 0.70 mm bite damage limit, cut-position/squareness limits, and final clearance. Candidate uses energy/velocity/stroke bounds and two safe cycles, but leaves rebound, overload, locking torque, and drift tolerance undeclared.
comparisons.reason: Both require iterative adjustment and regrasping, but cutting progression around a tube and avoiding workpiece deformation are materially different from tuning damping through measured stop dynamics and verifying lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Bread all faces of a chicken tender while minimizing destructive regrips; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires pressing, turning a compliant articulated food item and choosing sparse grasps. Candidate requires rigid small-tool manipulation, counterholding and fine rotary adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Record scores remaining bare surface area and final rack placement. Candidate scores dynamic carriage behavior and setting retention, with several limits unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Surface coverage and regrasp planning on a semi-deformable item are unrelated to damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Reinstall a dishwasher lower filter and quarter-turn-lock its upper filter; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both include alignment followed by retained rotation. Record requires placing a broad filter under tabs, inserting a cup and rotating lugs past a detent; candidate requires hex-key unlocking, fine setting rotation, relocking and impact-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Record checks filter pose, lug angle, detent passage, clearance and stillness. Candidate checks dynamic stopping and post-lock retention; rebound, overload and drift thresholds are undeclared.
comparisons.reason: Insertion and bayonet locking are materially different from adjusting a continuous parameter and validating its dynamic effect.

comparisons.objective: Measure a subfloor gap with a straightedge and wedge, then classify PASS or FAIL; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires placing a long straightedge, probing with a tapered gauge and making a classification. Candidate requires fine mechanical adjustment, locking and repeated impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Record checks straightedge support, wedge contact/readout and correct tag. Candidate checks energy absorption and setting retention, with some numeric response criteria missing.
comparisons.reason: Dimensional inspection and tagging test measurement placement rather than actuator commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Seat a slide member through a correctly positioned ball retainer; candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber through repeated impact trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rail alignment and rolling insertion versus hex-key engagement, setscrew release, fine collar rotation, relocking, and response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Rail must meet the forward retainer correctly and reach home; candidate requires two safe, repeatable ≥0.85 J stops within 12 mm stroke and a post-lock drift test.
comparisons.reason: The tested mechanisms and feedback loops differ meaningfully. Both involve alignment and pushing, but the slide task does not test adjustment, locking torque, or dynamic damping. Candidate rubric still lacks numeric collar-drift, excessive-rebound, and overload thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Install a piston through a ring compressor while holding the compressor down; candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual axial pressing and compressor hold-down versus recessed hex-key use, counterholding, collar rotation, torque-limited relocking, and iterative impact observation.
comparisons.success_condition: All rings must cross without compressor lift or escape and the piston must seat; candidate requires two non-bottoming, non-rebounding stops and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual stabilization and force control are generic primitives; the piston task tests simultaneous hold-down during insertion, not adjustable damping or repeated response-guided tuning. Candidate numeric drift/rebound/overload limits remain undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Route a retained cable through posts and seat its final clip; candidate commissions a compact shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable cable shaping, slack management, and clip seating versus rigid tool insertion, setscrew manipulation, collar adjustment, and controlled tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable must remain in the first clip, follow the permitted route, seat in both clips, and be released; candidate requires two physically simulated safe impact stops plus a locked-setting witness test.
comparisons.reason: The cable record tests deformable routing and retention, while the candidate tests mechanical adjustment and dynamic response. No meaningful duplication follows from bimanual coordination alone. Candidate omits numeric drift, rebound, and overload thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Extract a fitted collar with a prepared screw puller, recover it and park the tool; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require bimanual stabilization and repeated rotary actuation. Record turns a coarse screw to generate axial extraction, then transports a loaded tool; candidate unlocks and finely rotates an adjustment collar, relocks it and evaluates impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Record checks at least two screw turns, shaft clearance, jaw retention, collar recovery and stable tool parking. Candidate checks two acceptable stops and lock holding; response thresholds are partly unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Shared screw turning and counterholding are generic; force-driven extraction and dynamic parameter tuning have different objectives and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Tare an analytical balance and dispense exactly 1.00 g without spills; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires door operation, vessel placement, controlled granular pouring and button actuation. Candidate requires key alignment, collar adjustment, torque-limited locking and impact iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Record scores mass error, valid tare state, door closure and containment. Candidate scores dynamic stopping and retained adjustment, with several thresholds undeclared.
comparisons.reason: Precision material dosing is unrelated to mechanical energy-absorption tuning.

comparisons.objective: Disinfect an IV hub for 15 seconds before attaching and operating a syringe; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires sustained rubbing contact, ordered connector approach and syringe manipulation. Candidate requires recessed hex-key use, counterholding, collar adjustment and dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Record enforces 15 seconds of valid scrubbing before any syringe contact and then connection/flush stages. Candidate enforces repeated non-bottoming stops and retained setting; some numeric thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Procedural surface decontamination and medical connection test different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Ratchet a strap taut, latch its handle and retain a crate through a deck jolt; candidate tunes and locks a damper before impact trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both combine repeated rotary/oscillatory adjustment, locking and a later dynamic load test. Record requires large ratchet strokes and strap tensioning; candidate requires recessed key insertion, continuous fine collar tuning and settings inferred from stopping response.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires at least 50 N tension, closed handle and limited crate motion during a prescribed jolt. Candidate requires two non-bottoming carriage stops within a damper envelope and low setting drift, though rebound, overload and drift limits are undeclared.
comparisons.reason: Despite a similar adjust-lock-test structure, the tested manipulation and physical quantity differ materially: load restraint tension versus damping calibration.

comparisons.objective: Finish painting only bare panel regions while avoiding excess repainting and table contamination; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires roller contact control, coverage planning and avoidance of already-painted areas. Candidate requires precision tool engagement, fine retained rotation and iterative dynamic observation.
comparisons.success_condition: Record scores bare-cell coverage, wasted overlap and forbidden paint contact. Candidate scores stopping behavior and lock retention, with several response thresholds unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Selective surface coverage tests a fundamentally different physical ability from mechanical adjustment and commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Assemble and pulse a mini chopper; candidate tunes and locks an axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Blade-on-pin insertion and bayonet lid locking versus recessed-key engagement, fine collar rotation, torque-limited setscrew locking, and response-based retuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct assembly and powered pulse without blade contact versus two non-bottoming impact cycles and post-lock stability.
comparisons.reason: Both include bimanual stabilization and rotary locking, but these generic primitives support different tested abilities; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Safely isolate, disconnect, and blank a pneumatic line; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Valve/padlock/dump operation, collet depression, tube extraction, and plug insertion versus tool-based unlock-adjust-relock and dynamic-response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Depressurized, disconnected, plugged port with supply isolated versus repeated carriage stops without hard-stop strike, overload, rebound, or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: All eight indexed spec versions were read, including the lock-and-bleed variants; the candidate does not test pneumatic release or blanking.

comparisons.objective: Perform a two-hand keyboard passage with controlled dynamics and timing; candidate tunes mechanical damping.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated key striking at different speeds and durations versus hex-key insertion, counterholding, fine rotary adjustment, and tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct notes, timing, velocity separation, releases, and hand clearance versus two safe physical impact responses and locked-setting retention.
comparisons.reason: Shared force modulation is only a generic primitive; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Break a jar seal, unscrew the lid while counterholding the jar, and set the lid down; candidate tunes and secures a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lever insertion, prying, counter-torque, lid twisting, and placement versus hex-key alignment, setscrew release, fine retained-collar rotation, relocking, and iterative impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Seal break, 80° loosening rotation, safe lid removal, placement, and spill/tilt avoidance versus two repeatable stops without stroke, hard-stop, rebound, overload, or drift failures.
comparisons.reason: Although both use bimanual counterholding and rotation, the jar tests sequential seal release and removal; the candidate tests calibrated adjustment retained by a setscrew and judged through repeated dynamics. Candidate drift/rebound/overload thresholds are not numerically specified.

comparisons.objective: Pose helping-hands arms so two wire ends cross at a mark; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual manipulation of friction-jointed linkages and precise wire alignment versus tool engagement, collar adjustment, locking torque, and iterative dynamic diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified wire overlap, gap, mark position, stillness, and release versus bounded travel and repeatable non-bottoming carriage stops.
comparisons.reason: The record tests articulated spatial alignment, not adjustment from impact response; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Start a thread with a tap wrench and back off to break the chip; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Symmetric two-handle torque while maintaining tap squareness versus counterholding a small damper, recessed-key work, fine collar rotation, and response-guided retuning.
comparisons.success_condition: 90° forward then at least 36° reverse without side-load, tilt, or stripping versus two acceptable impact cycles and post-lock drift control.
comparisons.reason: Rotary force control is shared, but the tested abilities—thread cutting versus dynamic commissioning—are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Identify, unlatch, withdraw, support, and place the named drawout relay; candidate commissions and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Handle-latch release, guided heavy extraction, bimanual load support, and placement versus small-tool insertion, counterholding, fine rotation, bounded tightening, and iterative control actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct relay must be removed and placed upright without touching the other relay or entering the case; candidate must achieve two safe repeatable stops and retain its setting under witness torque.
comparisons.reason: Both include release mechanisms and bimanual support, but the relay task tests selection and supported extraction rather than adjustment, torque control, and dynamic commissioning. Candidate numeric drift/rebound/overload limits are missing.

comparisons.objective: Insert a battery correctly and screw on a flashlight cap; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Polarity-aware insertion, thread starting, repeated regrasping, and cap tightening versus setscrew unlocking, collar tuning, and witness-tested relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Correctly oriented cell and cap seated after sufficient thread rotation versus safe repeated impacts within stroke and response limits.
comparisons.reason: Threaded assembly and damper calibration are not duplicates despite shared rotation and regrasping; all nine versions provide adequate rubric detail.

comparisons.objective: Crimp a terminal or lug onto a cable; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold cable at insertion depth and alignment while closing a press versus hex-key seating, counterholding, collar adjustment, and bounded locking torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Good aligned crimp, tool release, placement, and in one version a 450 N pull test versus two repeatable damped stops and setting retention.
comparisons.reason: Both use bimanual force control, but the functional transformations and verification are unrelated; all six versions were read.

comparisons.objective: Tighten a tourniquet to a target gauge reading and lock its windlass; candidate tunes a damper from impact response.
comparisons.physical_skill: Windlass turning, holding against spring-back, regrasping, gauge reading, and clip latching versus recessed-key work, collar micro-adjustment, counterholding, and setscrew torque.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 250 mmHg with rod clipped and hands clear versus two non-bottoming cycles at specified energy/velocity plus post-lock drift tolerance.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest feedback-and-lock pattern, but it tests reaching one static pressure target, not iterative dynamic-response commissioning; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Align a suction tool to a robot flange and lock it with a ring; candidate adjusts and relocks a robot-axis shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual plate alignment and support while actuating a lock lever versus hex-key seating, setscrew loosening, collar micro-rotation, retightening, and response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct tool must be pose-seated, ring-locked, hanging securely, released, and arms returned; candidate requires two safe impact cycles within a physical energy/velocity/stroke envelope and a lock-retention test.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record because both combine alignment, bimanual stabilization, and locking, but it tests attaching a tool, not changing and validating a damping parameter through physical cycles. Its simulated lock uses a switched fixed joint, unlike the candidate's required contact-bearing setscrew. Candidate drift/rebound/overload thresholds remain undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Install and set a blind rivet, dispose of its stem, and return the riveter; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rivet pickup/insertion, square tool holding, repeated handle pumping, and debris handling versus recessed-key use, retained-collar adjustment, torque-limited locking, and iterative dynamic observation.
comparisons.success_condition: Rivet must set without tilt or lift, stem must land in the tray, and tool must be returned; candidate requires two repeatable non-bottoming stops and no post-lock drift.
comparisons.reason: Both demand tool alignment and force control, but rivet setting is an irreversible joining operation with waste handling; it does not test parameter tuning or repeated impact response. Candidate lacks numeric drift, excessive-rebound, and overload thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Rock a named fuse from spring clips with an insulated puller; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select and operate a tong puller, grip the fuse body, lever each end free, and place it versus hex-key alignment, counterholding, collar tuning, and tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct fuse removed with the tool and placed without disturbing neighbors versus safe repeated impacts and stable post-lock adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Both involve small-tool engagement, but the tested extraction and commissioning abilities differ; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Gauge seven blocks in the required GO/NO-GO sequence and sort them by tolerance; candidate tunes and secures a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated part pickup, gauge alignment, contact-based fit classification, and sorting versus small-tool insertion, counterholding, fine rotary adjustment, locking torque, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Every block must receive valid gauge checks and reach the correct tray, with strong penalties for escapes; candidate requires two safe repeatable impact stops within published energy, velocity, and stroke limits plus lock retention.
comparisons.reason: The gauge task tests inspection-driven classification across multiple parts; the candidate tests closed-loop adjustment of one dynamic component. Shared contact sensing and alignment are generic only. Candidate numeric drift/rebound/overload criteria are still missing.

comparisons.objective: Safely zero a slicer gauge, release its carriage, and place the carriage on a cleaning tray; candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber through repeated impact trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Some shared knob rotation/regrasping, but slicer tests safety sequencing, multi-turn release, and bimanual carriage removal/carrying; candidate tests recessed hex-key engagement, collar counterholding, bounded locking torque, and response-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Slicer requires gauge ≤0.5 mm before carriage motion, release ≥1,060°, safe blade-zone avoidance, and flat tray placement. Candidate requires two repeatable ≥0.85 J cycles within stroke/rebound/overload limits plus post-lock drift resistance.
comparisons.reason: The shared rotary primitive does not test the same ability. Slicer fidelity omits real threads/gearing and uses a switched interlock; candidate instead depends on physical lock retention and dynamic damping behavior. Candidate still lacks a numeric collar-drift tolerance and manufacturer values for setscrew torque, friction, and damping-versus-setting.

comparisons.objective: Secure a gas cylinder to a bracket with a chain; candidate tunes an axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Wrap, tension, choose a link, and hook a chain while avoiding the valve versus small-tool alignment, counterholding, collar adjustment, and relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct chain height/snugness and restraint under a 10 N pull test versus repeated safe impact absorption and setting stability.
comparisons.reason: The retention mechanisms and tested load responses differ; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Align and secure a scaffold transom using a hinged coupler, swing bolt, and nut; candidate tunes and locks a damper for acceptable carriage dynamics.
comparisons.physical_skill: Scaffold tests supporting and aligning a 3.1 kg tube, closing a cap, swinging a bolt into a slot, and finger-running a nut with regrips. Candidate tests small recessed-tool insertion, counterholding, collar adjustment, force-limited relocking, and iterative impact-response judgment.
comparisons.success_condition: Scaffold requires mark within 10 mm, squareness/cap within 3°, bolt seated, and resistance to a 50 N pull. Candidate requires two compliant impact cycles and a post-lock witness-torque/drift check.
comparisons.reason: Both include bimanual stabilization and rotary fastening, but the scaffold's tested ability is large-part alignment followed by multi-element latching; the candidate's is closed-loop dynamic commissioning. Scaffold omits final podger torque and models its thread in code; candidate lacks a numeric drift tolerance and calibrated torque/damping data.

comparisons.objective: Remove a reject bin from a gravity lane while controlling the following bin; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load extraction and restraint/release of gravity-driven bins versus recessed tool use, fine rotation, counterholding, and iterative response evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Reject placed, following-bin motion bounded, lane closed, and no falls versus two bounded carriage stops with no hard-stop strike or rebound.
comparisons.reason: The record tests transient material-flow control, not component adjustment; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Release a screwdriver from a spring clamp and hold it at a target pose; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Retain the tool while releasing a spring jaw and counterholding a loose base versus use of a hex key as the active tool for unlock-adjust-relock work.
comparisons.success_condition: Tool clears the clamp and is held stably at the marker without drop or base displacement versus two repeatable impact stops and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: The common presence of a tool, spring, and counterholding is generic; the tested manipulation outcome is different.

comparisons.objective: Uncover a rice-cooker steam vent before starting it; candidate commissions an industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Move and stably place a towel, press and release a button, then withdraw versus tool alignment, fine rotary adjustment, tightening, and repeated guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Vent clear before COOK activation, towel supported, button released, and hands clear versus energy-qualified carriage stops without bottoming, overload, rebound, or drift.
comparisons.reason: The indexed spec references SCORING.md for finer support and validity bounds not included in the record, but the available objective and success rubric still establish a clear distinction.

comparisons.objective: Choose fitting tweezers and peel protective film while stabilizing a display carrier; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool selection, passive-tweezer actuation, tab pinching, controlled peeling, counterholding, and tool return versus hex-key engagement and collar commissioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Complete peel without excess carrier motion, film supported outside, tools correctly returned, and hands clear versus two acceptable impact cycles and retained setting.
comparisons.reason: Both demand bimanual stabilization and small-tool use, but the physical transformations and verification differ; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Selectively harvest ripe tomatoes at their knuckles; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compliant fruit grasping, bend-to-snap detachment, damage avoidance, and placement versus rigid-tool insertion, counterholding, fine rotation, and torque control.

comparisons.objective: Open a locker while supporting a case leaning on its door, then place the case upright; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain hidden-load support through door opening, transfer grasp, and upright placement versus recessed-key work, collar tuning, and dynamic inspection.
comparisons.success_condition: Case never tipped or dropped and ends standing released on the mat versus two safe impact cycles and post-lock setting stability.
comparisons.reason: The record tests support removal and load handling rather than adjustment; all six versions were read and their differing drop rule was considered.

comparisons.objective: Clamp and flatten a glued panel, not commission an impact damper through repeated cycles.
comparisons.physical_skill: Places and closes alternating bar clamps with force control; no hex-key unlocking, collar tuning, or dynamic-response iteration.

comparisons.objective: Assemble and tighten a pipe compression joint in the correct part order; candidate adjusts and locks a shock absorber based on repeated dynamic trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compression joint tests pipe seating, ordered olive/nut placement, spanner-on-flats alignment, repeated short tightening strokes, and tool return.
